correctness.rationale: For a zero-labelled cell, its open-neighbourhood sum is exactly its row sum plus column sum. A zero-sum row forces every column sum at least 2; otherwise either a weight-one row forces every column positive or all rows have weight at least two. This proves the sharp lower bound \(\min\{n,2m\}\). Equality imposes either one unit in every column and no empty row, or exactly two units in every row. Counting these with surjections and independent row compositions gives the formula, with exact intersection \(n!/(2!)^m\) at \(n=2m\). The one-cell boundary is valid. The independently coded verifier checked 1,152,264 complete assignments at 14 small orders and 696,634 assignments of weight at most the optimum at four other orders. The proof, not this finite enumeration, establishes all positive orders.

value.rationale: The exact natural labelled optimizer classification reveals a sharp transition between a surjection/Stirling-number family and independently row-heavy configurations, with a nontrivial overlap correction at \(n=2m\). It refines a recent motivation to count Italian dominating functions and pinpoints an ordinary-versus-perfect Italian domination gap on a fundamental Cartesian product graph class. Exact minimum multiplicity, not merely a renaming or known minimum, is useful for extremal structure and the least-weight coefficient of the Italian domination polynomial.
